axioms_are_definitional: reachability is axiomatised as the reflexive-transitive closure by the four clauses in closure_axioms, including a well-founded rank on justification. Transitive closure is not first-order definable, so those clauses are the definition used here and are not derived from anything more primitive.

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: SCOPE_NON_AMPLIFICATION
theorems.statement: for every judgment and action over any object universe, if the action is authorised then its scope is a subset of the judgment's scope
theorems.why_it_matters: the finite core checks this on two authored judgments over three named claims; this is the same statement with the universe left free

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: DOMAIN_CONFINEMENT
theorems.statement: an authorised action's domain is reachable from the judgment's domain through the registered conversion relation
theorems.why_it_matters: authority never arrives in a domain except along conversions someone registered; reaching a domain is always a licensed step, never a default

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: NO_LAUNDERING_GENERAL
theorems.statement: if no conversion is registered, an authorised action's domain equals the judgment's domain, for a domain sort of any cardinality
theorems.why_it_matters: this is the generalisation of the thirty-six-pair enumeration: the finite core asserts result is (source == target) over six authored domains, and the same claim holds here over all of them

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: NON_COMPENSATORY
theorems.statement: if any hard obligation is unmet, no configuration of issuer, scope, domain or epoch authorises the action
theorems.why_it_matters: a non-compensatory gate is the paper's central structural claim; if a strong enough elsewhere could outweigh an unmet obligation the whole authority argument collapses into a score

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: DEFEATER_MONOTONICITY
theorems.statement: activating a defeater can only remove authorisations, never create one
theorems.why_it_matters: revocation must be monotone or a revoked authority could be restored by revoking something else, which is the laundering shape one level up

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: EPOCH_ISOLATION
theorems.statement: an authorised action carries the judgment's epoch, so replay across epochs is impossible
theorems.why_it_matters: a judgment is authority about a state of the world, not a bearer token

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: ONE_STEP_LEMMA
theorems.statement: if a judgment delegates to a second and the second authorises an action, the first's scope contains the action's scope and the first's domain reaches the action's domain
theorems.why_it_matters: this is the induction step from which chain non-amplification follows for delegation graphs of unbounded depth

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: CONV_IMPLIES_REACH
theorems.statement: a registered conversion is itself a reach
theorems.why_it_matters: the bridge from the conversion relation to reachability; stated as its own lemma because the cycle theorem needs it and, proved together, the two were more than the solver would discharge

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: CYCLE_COLLAPSE
theorems.statement: if two domains reach each other then they reach exactly the same domains, so a cycle merges its members into one authority class
theorems.why_it_matters: the requested characterisation of cycles: a registered cycle is not a loophole that manufactures authority, it is a declaration that the domains it joins are authority-equivalent, and it says so in advance

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: ACYCLIC_STRICTNESS
theorems.statement: if reachability is antisymmetric --- the acyclic case --- then two distinct domains cannot each authorise action in the other
theorems.why_it_matters: names what acyclicity buys, so the general theorems are not silently credited with it: non-amplification holds either way, and antisymmetry is what additionally forbids mutual authority
